### Bind a reactive source to a mascot

`watch_mascot()` subscribes to a Shiny reactive expression or `reactiveVal()`
and forwards matching values to `update_mascot()`. Use a named character vector
when only moods change, or a named list for key-wise field overrides:

```{r watch_mascot-call, echo = FALSE}
htmltools::tags$pre(htmltools::tags$code(paste0(
  'ready <- shiny::reactive(isTRUE(input$ready))\n',
  'obs <- mascot::watch_mascot(\n',
  '  "helper",\n',
  '  ready,\n',
  '  list(\n',
  '    "TRUE" = list(mood = "happy", status = "Ready"),\n',
  '    "FALSE" = list(mood = "worried", status = "Missing required fields")\n',
  '  )\n',
  ')\n',
  '# Call obs$destroy() if you need to stop watching before the session ends.'
)))
```

Unmatched, `NA`, `NULL` and non-scalar values leave the mascot unchanged. Inside
a Shiny module, pass the local id just as in `update_mascot()`.

```{r watch_mascot-mistakes, echo = FALSE}
if (!in_studio()) guide_mistakes_html("watch_mascot", studio_character)
```
